name: Lattice
rationale: A lattice is a regular, repeating structure where nodes connect in predictable patterns — mirrors how Converge's DAG connects tasks into verifiable workflows. Mathematical precision meets structural clarity.
why_creative: Evokes both rigorous systems (crystal lattices, lattice graphs) and the interconnected nature of task dependencies without being literal.
risk: Somewhat technical, may feel academic rather than developer-friendly

name: Stratum
rationale: Geological layers that build upon each other, each verifiable and stable before the next forms. Captures the layered, foundational nature of task execution where each layer must pass checks.
why_creative: Strong, grounded metaphor for layered execution. Uncommon in dev tools but immediately understandable.
risk: Two valid pronunciations could cause confusion

name: Apex
rationale: The convergence point where all paths meet — the top of the DAG where all tasks complete and the final result emerges. Implies reaching the optimal solution.
why_creative: Short, punchy, implies peak performance and goal achievement. Works well as a CLI command.
risk: Used by Salesforce (Apex programming language), may have trademark conflicts

name: Vertex
rationale: A node in a graph where edges meet — the fundamental unit of a DAG. Each task is a vertex, each dependency an edge. Pure graph theory.
why_creative: Technically precise for DAG-based systems, sounds sharp and modern. Strong CLI feel.
risk: May feel too technical or academic for broader developer audience

name: Flux
rationale: Continuous flow and transformation — agents processing tasks, state flowing through the DAG, convergence emerging from dynamic execution.
why_creative: One syllable, dynamic energy, implies constant forward motion. Strong brand presence.
risk: Facebook's Flux architecture pattern may cause confusion in frontend contexts

name: Prism
rationale: Takes one input (a complex problem) and splits it into component parts (spectrum of tasks), then recombines them into a complete solution. Diverge-converge made visual.
why_creative: Beautiful metaphor for decomposition and recomposition. Memorable, ownable, premium feel.
risk: Prisma ORM is a major dev tool — too close for comfort

name: Kernel
rationale: The core computational unit that executes operations — in Converge's case, the runtime that orchestrates agents and verifies results. Essential, foundational, irreducible.
why_creative: Deeply technical credibility, implies low-level power and control. Familiar to developers.
risk: Heavily overloaded term (OS kernels, Jupyter kernels, ML kernels) — may lack distinctiveness

name: Catalyst
rationale: Enables reactions (task execution) without being consumed — the orchestration layer that makes agent work happen efficiently and repeatably.
why_creative: Implies acceleration and enablement. Strong metaphor for what orchestration does.
risk: Three syllables, slightly longer. Generic enough that trademark/domain may be contested

name: Helix
rationale: Spiral structure that iterates upward — like Converge's retry loops that spiral toward convergence, each attempt building on the last until checks pass.
why_creative: Elegant shape, implies progress through iteration. Distinctive and memorable.
risk: Perforce Helix is a version control system — potential confusion in dev tool space

name: Orbit
rationale: Stable, repeatable paths — like playbooks that run the same way every time. Tasks orbit around the goal until they lock into stable completion.
why_creative: Implies stability, predictability, and cyclical refinement. Clean, simple, ownable.
risk: May feel too abstract or disconnected from the concrete work of task execution

name: Pulse
rationale: Rhythmic execution — agents firing, tasks completing, checks running. The heartbeat of automated workflow.
why_creative: One syllable, energetic, implies life and continuous operation. Great CLI feel.
risk: Generic enough that many products use it — may be hard to own

name: Anchor
rationale: The stable foundation that holds everything in place — verified outputs that downstream tasks can depend on. Each completed task anchors the next.
why_creative: Implies reliability and trust. Strong metaphor for verified, cacheable task outputs.
risk: May feel static rather than dynamic — doesn't capture the execution/flow aspect

name: Substrate
rationale: The underlying layer on which reactions occur — the runtime foundation that agents execute upon. Technical precision for the orchestration layer.
why_creative: Uncommon in dev tools, technically credible, implies foundational infrastructure.
risk: Three syllables, may feel academic. Polkadot's Substrate framework exists in blockchain space

name: Vortex
rationale: Converging flow — all tasks spiral inward toward the final result. Dynamic, powerful, implies inevitable convergence.
why_creative: Strong visual metaphor, energetic, implies powerful convergence. Memorable and distinctive.
risk: May feel chaotic rather than controlled — doesn't emphasize verification/reliability

name: Axis
rationale: The central line around which everything rotates — the core orchestration logic that all tasks revolve around. Foundational, structural, essential.
why_creative: Short, sharp, implies centrality and structure. Strong CLI command feel.
risk: Generic term, may be hard to trademark. Doesn't strongly evoke the DAG/workflow concept
